# Plan: Build the opening environment and terminal

## Design

Source context: `index.html` has `#app` and loads `src/main.ts`; `three` is in `package.json`; `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts` serves the build under `/signal-lost/`; `.swarm/architecture.md` names the `app`, `render`, `terminal`, and `input` modules.

- `src/app/scenes.ts`: DOM-free `createSceneManager()`. A `Scene` has `mount(): void` and `dispose(): void`. `show(scene)` disposes the current scene before mounting the next one; `dispose()` tears down the current one. Pure, unit-tested.
- `src/app/opening.ts`: opening scene. Prints the design's SIGNAL RECEIVED text line by line, then the prompt. Enter or a click at any time moves on. Removes its listeners on dispose.
- `src/app/hub.ts`: boot sequence and terminal hub. Prints the OBSERVER NETWORK boot text, then a numbered tool menu from a `Tool[]` list. Tools are `{ id, label, run }`. This WorkUnit ships only real ones (`STATUS`, `HELP`); later WorkUnits add theirs. No placeholder entries.
- `src/terminal/terminal.ts`: DOM terminal. `print(lines)`, `menu(items)`, and a command input. Output goes in a `role="log"` `aria-live="polite"` element as real text. Menu items are buttons, also chosen by typing the number or name.
- `src/render/environment.ts`: Three.js scene, loaded by dynamic import so text appears before the 3D code does. Starfield `Points`, a flat-shaded low-poly icosahedron with a ring, a moving analyzer sweep line, low-resolution rendering with pixelated CSS scaling, vertex snapping by `onBeforeCompile`. `createEnvironment(canvas, { motion })` returns `{ start, stop, setMotion, dispose }`, or throws when WebGL is unavailable. Rendering stops when the document is hidden and on `stop`/`dispose`, which also disposes geometries, materials and the renderer. `motion: false` renders one still frame.
- `src/main.ts`: bootstraps. If the environment throws, it sets `document.body.dataset.render = 'fallback'` and shows a CSS-only static starfield; otherwise `'webgl'`. The game continues either way.
- `src/style.css`: CRT bezel, amber phosphor, subtle scanlines and vignette, and periodic interference as a CSS animation on an overlay. System monospace stack, because no font asset is in the repo.

Opening and boot text are fixed interface text in `src/app/text.ts`. Story content starts in the Episode 000 WorkUnit.

## Files

New: `src/app/{scenes,opening,hub,text}.ts`, `src/terminal/terminal.ts`, `src/render/environment.ts`, `src/style.css`, `tests/unit/scenes.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts`. Changed: `src/main.ts`, `index.html` only if the stylesheet link needs it, `tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts` (the old text expectation still applies), `playwright.config.ts` (add a software WebGL launch flag so tests can exercise the real renderer).

## Edge cases

- Enter pressed before the opening finishes still boots.
- WebGL failing at context creation shows the fallback with no uncaught error.
- A dynamic-import or render failure also uses the fallback.
- Resizing updates the renderer size.

## Out of scope

Puzzles, audio, persistence, settings UI.

# Test plan

| Acceptance criterion | Verification | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opening shows starfield, rotating object, sweep, interference and the text, ending in the prompt | `tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts`: text and prompt visible, `body[data-render=webgl]`, canvas has non-blank pixels, interference overlay present. Source inspection of `environment.ts` for the scene elements. | Developer on host; CI `Browser tests` |
| Enter or click boots into a terminal with a tool menu | `opening.spec.ts`, once with Enter and once with click, then a menu button works and a typed command works | Developer on host; CI |
| WebGL failure shows a styled fallback and stays playable | `opening.spec.ts` forces `getContext` to return null by init script: `data-render=fallback`, no page errors, boot still works | Developer on host; CI |
| Lifecycle mounts and disposes scenes, rendering stops when not needed | `npx vitest run tests/unit/scenes.test.ts`; source inspection of `stop`/`dispose` and the visibility handling | Developer; tester inspects |
| Browser tests cover opening, boot, fallback under the subpath | `fixtures.ts` returns 404 outside `/signal-lost/`; `opening.spec.ts` uses it | CI |

## Roles

- **Developer:** runs focused commands above and `npm run lint`. Browser specs run on the host session, as sandboxes cannot start Chromium (`.swarm/rules/lessons.md`).
- **Tester:** independently inspects source against the criteria, reuses applicable passing results, repeats only for relevant changes, failures, or unresolved coverage.
- **Coordinator:** alone runs the complete required policy. The `Browser tests` workflow on the PR is the browser evidence.
